record.context_brief: Serre-invariant stability on the Veronese double cone
record.original_question: Let Y1 be the prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1, equivalently the degree-6 hypersurface in the weighted projective space P(1,1,1,2,3) known as the Veronese double cone. Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on Ku(Y1) under the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)?

evidence.quote: We denote by Yd a prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1 <= d <= 5 and take its Kuznetsov component Ku(Yd ) := <OYd , OYd (HYd )>^perp.
Recall that Y1 is a hypersurface of degree 6 in the weighted projective space P(1, 1, 1, 2, 3), known as the Veronese double cone.
Question 5.32. Is there a unique GL 2 f+ (R)-orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on Ku(Y1 )?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y_1$ denote the smooth prime Fano threefold of Picard rank one, index two, and degree one, equivalently realized as a smooth hypersurface of degree $6$ in the weighted projective space $\mathbb{P}(1,1,1,2,3)$ (the Veronese double cone). Let $\mathcal{D}^b(Y_1)$ be its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves, and let $\mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(H)$ denote the polarization corresponding to the ample generator $H$ of $\operatorname{Pic}(Y_1)$. Define the Kuznetsov component
$$\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1) := \langle \mathcal{O}_{Y_1},\, \mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(H) \rangle^{\perp} \subset \mathcal{D}^b(Y_1),$$
i.e. the right orthogonal of the exceptional pair $(\mathcal{O}_{Y_1}, \mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(H))$. Let $S_{\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)}$ be the Serre functor of $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$. Recall that a Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma$ on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ is called Serre-invariant if $S_{\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)} \cdot \sigma$ lies in the orbit of $\sigma$ under the action of $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$, the universal cover of $\mathrm{GL}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$, on the space of stability conditions.

Question: Do all Serre-invariant Bridgeland stability conditions on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ form a single orbit under the action of $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$?
artifact.status_search_result: For prime Fano threefolds $Y_d$ of index two and degree $2\le d\le 5$, uniqueness of the $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$-orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_d)$ has been established via the fractional Calabi–Yau criterion of Feyzbakhsh–Pertusi and Pertusi–Yang. For $d=1$ (the Veronese double cone), recent work on categorical Torelli theorems for weighted hypersurfaces explicitly mentions that the orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ is not known to be unique and that this is a motivation for using Hochschild–Serre algebra methods instead. No definitive proof of uniqueness or non-uniqueness for $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ was located, so the status is reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: IVHS via Kuznetsov components and categorical Torelli theorems for weighted hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: the orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions is not unique, so the moduli space constructed from Ku(Y) is not canonical
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on the Veronese double cone notes that uniqueness of the orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on Ku(Y_1) is not established and motivates alternative (Hochschild–Serre algebra) techniques.

status_evidence.title: Serre-invariant stability conditions and Ulrich bundles on cubic threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: a fractional Calabi–Yau category of dimension at most 2 admits a unique Serre-invariant stability condition, up to the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)
status_evidence.claim: A general fractional Calabi–Yau criterion gives uniqueness of Serre-invariant stability conditions in related cases (e.g. cubic threefolds), but its applicability to Y_1 is not confirmed in the literature located.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Kuznetsov component of the Veronese double cone
status_evidence.snippet: moduli space of stable complexes in the Kuznetsov component of the Veronese double cone
status_evidence.claim: Work on Ku(Y_1) addresses moduli of stable complexes but does not resolve uniqueness of the Serre-invariant stability orbit.
